plan.title: Integrate ordered isolated-guest input-cold status collection

criteria.description: Cold collection requires a live controller reset callback and matching Linux/root boot identity, not a JSON assertion. Portable protocol tests prove sync/reset/two nonresident probes/closed probe descriptors/guarded collector ordering, fixed 100ms probe-finish-to-collector-start bound, rejection of reset failure, resident or invalid probes, identity changes and cleanup failures. A narrow controller-only probe-fd exception does not authorize external descriptors or mappings.

Measurement accepts cold mode only through its controller API with reader guard required, uses zero cold warmups and per-sample reset, preserves one warm-cache warmup and existing macOS/first-run paths, validates expected passing status and post-sample provenance, and emits manifest-bound raw status/timing/transition evidence only after all samples succeed. Public CLI cold requests remain rejected.

Existing real warm/first-run status smoke remains passing. Separately, before task closure an approved isolated disposable Linux guest must execute small guarded warm and cold workloads with source/binary hashes, boot/environment evidence and fixed gap bound; ordinary CI never resets caches.

limitations: E03b-3 only, no P11 thirty-sample results, new dependency, toolchain installation, release or general-host cache-reset command. The public helper has no built-in reset backend or JSON/environment-variable unlock. Actual reset is supplied by the host-verified private disposable-VM controller; guest root and a claimed UUID alone are insufficient isolation evidence. Strict cold means observed nonresident input file pages before collector launch, not cold host/hypervisor/storage caches or an atomic snapshot. Shell handoff and observer overhead remain timed; the fixed 100ms gap is not a latency SLA or proof against later readers. Existing fd/mmap/provenance limitations persist. The coherent integration may exceed 300 implementation lines because probe-fd lifetime, collector timing, measurement API and their fault tests share one rollback boundary.
